entries.title: II Kings 6:1
segments:
The place; the building or apartment they occupied. 
 
  Strait; narrow, small.

entries.title: II Kings 6:5
segments: Borrowed articles should be used with care, and in due time returned, uninjured, to the owner.

entries.title: II Kings 6:13
segments: Dothan; a place a few miles north of Samaria,

entries.title: II Kings 6:14
segments: Wicked men often hope to prevail against those who have God for their protector, but all such hopes are vain.

entries.title: II Kings 6:16
segments: They that be with us; God, and all the heavenly hosts.

entries.title: II Kings 6:17
segments: All who have right views will see that the servants of God, however great their apparent danger, are perfectly safe under his care.

entries.title: II Kings 6:18
segments: This people; the hosts of the king of Syria.

entries.title: II Kings 6:22
segments:
Wouldest thou smite those; he would not; and much less should he smite those who had been miraculously delivered into his power. 
 
Kindness towards enemies is good policy, as well as a Christian duty; however it may be received, will be the means of good to those who exercise it.

entries.title: II Kings 6:25
segments:
Pieces; shekels. 
 
  A cab; between one and two quarts. 
 
  Dove's dung; supposed by many to be a mean kind of pulse or pea, called by that name. 
 
None but God can fully understand the evils of war, or the guilt of those who are instrumental in needlessly inflicting them upon their fellow men.

entries.title: II Kings 6:31
segments: If the head of Elisha--shall stand on him; he considered Elisha as the cause of the famine, or as guilty in not removing it.  Many suppose that the prophet had promised him deliverance from the Syrians, and that he was vexed at the delay, and ready to destroy Elisha as a deceiver.  See note to

. 
 
Those who foretell the calamity of the wicked, are often treated as it they were the cause of it, and as if their removal would prevent the coming or continuance of threatened evils; but all expectations of relief in that way will be disappointed.

entries.title: II Kings 6:33
segments: What should I wait for the Lord; the exclamation of the king, who immediately followed his messenger to the door of Elisha; implying that God was his enemy, that the promised deliverance was no longer to be hoped for, and that confidence in Jehovah was a vain thing.
